app.uiRule: Show the primary value plus a descriptive CFG value and all relevant vanilla difficulty reference values.

source.dumpLabel: Current extracted base GameData + DLC1 CFG baseline (2026-10-02)

scope.environmentPolicy: Tune anomaly gameplay effects only; do not tune weather or emission occurrence.

parameters.label: Human Enemy Health
parameters.description: Changes how much damage human enemies can take before they die.
parameters.rationale: Changes how much damage human enemies can take before they die.
parameters.logic: Higher values make human enemies tougher and gunfights longer. Lower values make them go down faster. This does not change how much damage they deal.
parameters.interaction: Your Weapon Damage affects the same time-to-kill from the opposite side. Raising enemy health while lowering your weapon damage compounds the effect.

parameters.label: Human Enemy Gun Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage you take from firearm hits by human enemies.
parameters.rationale: Changes how much damage you take from firearm hits by human enemies.
parameters.logic: Higher values make successful enemy shots hurt more. Lower values make gunfire less punishing. Vanilla ranges from very forgiving on Novice to substantially harder on Master.
parameters.interaction: Human Enemy Health controls how long enemies survive; this controls how dangerous their shots are. Repeated-Hit Protection can also affect how sustained incoming fire feels.

parameters.label: Human Attack Frequency
parameters.description: Controls how frequently human enemies can make another attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls how frequently human enemies can make another attack.
parameters.logic: 100% is vanilla. Above 100% shortens the underlying attack cooldown and makes attacks more frequent; below 100% lengthens the cooldown and gives you more breathing room. This does not change weapon fire rate or burst length.
parameters.interaction: Combine this with Human Enemy Gun Damage and Human Enemy Fire Accuracy to shape how relentless human firefights feel.

parameters.label: Human Enemy Fire Accuracy
parameters.description: Changes the accuracy of human enemy gunfire through the game's exposed fire-accuracy multiplier.
parameters.rationale: Changes the accuracy of human enemy gunfire through the game's exposed fire-accuracy multiplier.
parameters.logic: Higher values make human gunfire more accurate; lower values make it less accurate. Vanilla keeps this at 100% on every difficulty.
parameters.interaction: This player-facing control maps to the CFG HipAccuracyMultiplier field. It does not represent mutant attacks, melee, grenade use, or every internal AI aiming rule. Pair it with Human Enemy Gun Damage when tuning firefights.

parameters.label: Mutant Hit Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage mutant attacks deal when they connect.
parameters.rationale: Changes how much damage mutant attacks deal when they connect.
parameters.logic: Higher values make mutant hits more punishing; lower values make them more forgiving. Vanilla goes from 35% on Novice to 150% on Master.
parameters.interaction: Mutant Attack Frequency changes general attack frequency. Master-only special-ability cooldowns are tuned separately in the Master tab.

parameters.label: Mutant Attack Frequency
parameters.description: Controls how frequently mutants can make another general attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls how frequently mutants can make another general attack.
parameters.logic: 100% is vanilla. Above 100% shortens the underlying mutant attack cooldown and makes attacks more frequent; below 100% lengthens the cooldown and creates longer gaps. Vanilla uses 100% on all four standard difficulties.
parameters.interaction: Mutant Hit Damage controls how hard attacks land. Master-only species special-ability cooldowns are separate controls.

parameters.label: Your Weapon Damage
parameters.description: Changes the base damage dealt by your weapons.
parameters.rationale: Changes the base damage dealt by your weapons.
parameters.logic: Higher values make your weapons hit harder; lower values make enemies take more shots to kill. This applies before separate headshot and weapon-specific behavior.
parameters.interaction: Your Headshot Damage adds another layer on headshots. Human Enemy Health also changes the final time-to-kill.

parameters.label: Your Headshot Damage
parameters.description: Changes the damage multiplier applied when your weapon hit is a headshot.
parameters.rationale: Changes the damage multiplier applied when your weapon hit is a headshot.
parameters.logic: Higher values multiply headshot damage more strongly without directly changing body-shot damage. 100% is a neutral 1.0x multiplier; Master is the only vanilla difficulty that raises this field, to 2.0x.
parameters.interaction: Your Weapon Damage still affects the underlying hit, so raising both settings makes headshots much more lethal.

parameters.label: Weapon Jamming Frequency
parameters.description: Controls how often weapon jams occur through the difficulty multiplier.
parameters.rationale: Controls how often weapon jams occur through the difficulty multiplier.
parameters.logic: Higher values make jams more frequent; lower values make them less frequent. Master raises this multiplier to 150%.
parameters.interaction: Weapon condition and each weapon's own jam thresholds still matter. This control changes the difficulty-wide jamming frequency multiplier; it does not replace weapon-specific jam rules.

parameters.label: Explosion Damage
parameters.description: Changes damage from explosions such as grenades and other explosive effects.
parameters.rationale: Changes damage from explosions such as grenades and other explosive effects.
parameters.logic: Higher values make explosions more lethal; lower values make them more forgiving. It does not change bullet damage or anomaly damage.
parameters.interaction: Each explosion still has its own base damage. This setting scales the difficulty layer applied on top of those base values.

parameters.label: Repeated-Hit Protection — Maximum
parameters.description: Sets the stronger end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale: Sets the stronger end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.logic: Higher values mean stronger repeated-hit protection and generally easier sustained incoming fire. Lower values reduce that protection. This number is a strength setting, not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
parameters.interaction: Use it together with Repeated-Hit Protection — Minimum. Human Enemy Gun Damage still controls the damage of each individual bullet hit.

parameters.label: Repeated-Hit Protection — Minimum
parameters.description: Sets the weaker end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale: Sets the weaker end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.logic: Higher values mean more protection at the weak end of the system; lower values make repeated hits harsher. This number is a strength setting, not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
parameters.interaction: Use it together with Repeated-Hit Protection — Maximum. For a vanilla-like setup, keep Minimum at or below Maximum.

parameters.label: Healed Damage Still Counts
parameters.description: Controls whether damage remains in the repeated-hit protection tracker after you heal it.
parameters.rationale: Repeated-hit protection tracks damage taken over time. When this is ON, healing restores your HP but does not immediately erase that healed damage from the protection tracker, so earlier hits can still contribute to repeated-hit protection. When it is OFF, healed damage no longer remains part of that tracked damage. This does not reduce healing strength or make medkits restore less health.
parameters.logic: OFF matches Novice and Stalker. ON matches Veteran and Master. Healing always restores HP normally; this toggle only decides whether the healed portion is still remembered by the repeated-hit protection system.
parameters.interaction: Works with the Minimum and Maximum repeated-hit protection settings. The exact internal curve is not exposed by the CFG files.

parameters.label: Mutant Health
parameters.description: Adjust the health multipliers for the eight audited mutant families from one combined radar.

notes: Directly scales the authored MaxHP field in GameData/ObjPrototypes.cfg.
1x is vanilla.
This is not selected through DifficultyPrototypes.cfg; the same generated MaxHP applies regardless of the in-game difficulty.
Placed immediately next to the corresponding mutant Special Ability Cooldown control in Combat.

parameters.rationale: These eight confirmed direct MaxHP controls share the same 0.25x–3x multiplier model, so one radar makes mutant toughness easy to compare while preserving every original MaxHP writer route.
parameters.logic: Each axis is the existing authored MaxHP multiplier. 1x is vanilla; the legend shows both the multiplier and the effective audited MaxHP.
parameters.interaction: Drag one point to change only that mutant family. Right-click resets that family to 1x; R resets all eight Mutant Health values.

parameters.label: Mutant Special Attack Cooldown
parameters.description: Adjust the special-ability cooldown multipliers for the eight audited mutant families from one combined radar.

notes: Master explicitly defines 0.5 overrides; Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no agent override block and are represented as neutral 1.0 in the UI. Generated override insertion into Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: All eight cooldown controls share the same 0.25x–2x wait-time multiplier model and vanilla difficulty profile, so one radar makes special-ability pressure easy to compare without changing any writer route.
parameters.logic: Each axis is the actual wait-time multiplier: lower values make special abilities return sooner; higher values give more breathing room. Vanilla is 1x on Novice/Stalker/Veteran and 0.5x on Master.
parameters.interaction: Drag one point to change only that mutant family. Right-click resets that family to the currently selected Base Preset; R resets all eight cooldowns to the selected Base Preset.

parameters.label: Psy Phantom Spawn-Cycle Delay
parameters.description: Controls how long Psy encounters using the Master override wait before another phantom spawn cycle can begin.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls how long Psy encounters using the Master override wait before another phantom spawn cycle can begin.
parameters.logic: Lower percentages mean new phantom waves can return sooner. Master uses 50% of the normal wait time; 100% represents no extra Master override.
parameters.interaction: Psy Phantom Count controls how many phantoms are added per cycle. Shorter delays and higher counts compound quickly.

parameters.label: Psy Phantom Count
parameters.description: Controls how many Psy phantoms the Master override adds to the affected encounters.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls how many Psy phantoms the Master override adds to the affected encounters.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps the normal count. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles the configured phantom count.
parameters.interaction: Spawn-Cycle Delay changes how quickly another wave can happen; this setting changes the size of each wave.

parameters.label: Psy Phantoms Cause Bleeding
parameters.description: Lets the affected Master Psy phantoms inflict bleeding in addition to their normal threat.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Lets the affected Master Psy phantoms inflict bleeding in addition to their normal threat.
parameters.logic: OFF keeps this extra bleeding rule disabled. ON matches the Master override.
parameters.interaction: Bleeding Effect Strength and bleeding treatment still control how dangerous and recoverable the resulting bleeding is.

parameters.label: Psy Equipment Durability Damage
parameters.description: Controls how much equipment durability the affected Master Psy enemies damage.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls how much equipment durability the affected Master Psy enemies damage.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps normal durability damage. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles this durability damage.
parameters.interaction: This does not change their direct health damage. Armor/helmet durability settings still affect how your gear wears overall.

parameters.label: Hunger Build-up Rate
parameters.description: Controls how quickly the player's HungerPoints accumulate from the base player game rule.
parameters.rationale: Controls how quickly the player's HungerPoints accumulate from the base player game rule.
parameters.logic: Higher values make hunger build faster; lower values stretch the time between hunger states. Zero effectively stops passive hunger build-up.
parameters.interaction: Vanilla hunger states still decide when their effects become active. Food Fullness Effect and consumables determine how quickly hunger is pushed back down.

parameters.label: Hunger Stamina Recovery Penalty
parameters.description: Controls how strongly medium hunger reduces stamina recovery.
parameters.rationale: Controls the magnitude of the stamina-recovery penalty applied during medium hunger. The UI stores a positive penalty magnitude; the CFG stores the effect as a negative regeneration modifier.
parameters.logic: Higher values reduce stamina recovery more strongly while medium hunger is active. Zero removes this standard hunger recovery penalty. The writer converts the positive UI magnitude to the game CFG negative modifier.
parameters.interaction: This modifies regeneration, not the direct stamina cost of sprinting, jumping or melee.

parameters.label: Severe Hunger Stamina Recovery Penalty
parameters.description: Controls how strongly severe hunger reduces stamina recovery.
parameters.rationale: Controls the magnitude of the stamina-recovery penalty applied during severe hunger. The UI stores a positive penalty magnitude; the CFG stores the effect as a negative regeneration modifier.
parameters.logic: Higher values reduce stamina recovery more strongly while severe hunger is active. Zero removes this standard severe-hunger recovery penalty. The writer converts the positive UI magnitude to the game CFG negative modifier.
parameters.interaction: Master Starvation Mechanics can add further stamina drain on top of this standard severe-hunger penalty.

parameters.label: Fatigue Build-up Rate
parameters.description: Controls how quickly SleepinessPoints accumulate on the player.
parameters.rationale: Controls how quickly SleepinessPoints accumulate on the player.
parameters.logic: Higher values make fatigue build faster; lower values extend the time before sleepiness states are reached.
parameters.interaction: Vanilla fatigue states still decide when their penalties become active. Energy drinks can reduce accumulated fatigue separately.

parameters.label: Energy Drink Fatigue Relief
parameters.description: Scales the amount of accumulated fatigue removed by energy-drink sleepiness-reduction effects.

notes: Runtime EffectPrototypes.cfg exposes direct energy-drink SleepinessPoints relief (-20), the Weird Kettle limited-energy alternative (-100), and Poppy Field energy-drink regeneration effects (-3.5 and -5.0).
The slider scales only those energy-drink fatigue-relief values; passive player RegenSleepinessPoints remains controlled separately by Fatigue Build-up Rate.

parameters.rationale: Lets the player tune how strongly energy drinks counter fatigue without changing how quickly fatigue naturally accumulates.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla relief. 50% halves the mapped fatigue reduction, 200% doubles it, and 0% removes the mapped energy-drink fatigue relief.
parameters.interaction: Fatigue Build-up Rate controls passive SleepinessPoints accumulation. This control changes only the mapped energy-drink relief effects, including their special Poppy Field and Weird Kettle variants.

parameters.label: Sleep Becomes Available At
parameters.description: Controls how tired the player must be before normal sleeping is allowed.
parameters.rationale: Controls how tired the player must be before normal sleeping is allowed.
parameters.logic: Higher values require more accumulated sleepiness before sleep becomes available; lower values allow sleeping earlier.
parameters.interaction: Separate no-sleep effects from hunger, bleeding, radiation or Psy can still block sleep regardless of this threshold.

parameters.label: Minimum Sleep
parameters.description: Sets the minimum sleep duration used by the default sleep settings.
parameters.rationale: Sets the minimum sleep duration used by the default sleep settings.
parameters.logic: Higher values force a longer minimum rest period; lower values allow shorter sleep sessions.
parameters.interaction: This is a time requirement, not a direct setting for how much each restorative effect heals.

parameters.label: Radiation Accumulation
parameters.description: Scales the rate at which radiation is accumulated through the difficulty preset.
parameters.rationale: Scales the rate at which radiation is accumulated through the difficulty preset.
parameters.logic: Higher values make radiation exposure build faster; lower values make equivalent exposure accumulate more slowly.
parameters.interaction: Radiation Recovery controls passive reduction separately. Master Radiation Mechanics can also add a stamina penalty at high radiation.

parameters.label: Radiation Recovery
parameters.description: Controls the player's base radiation degeneration/recovery rate.
parameters.rationale: Controls the player's base radiation degeneration/recovery rate.
parameters.logic: Higher values clear accumulated radiation faster; lower values make radiation persist longer.
parameters.interaction: This acts on recovery, not exposure strength. Radiation Accumulation determines how quickly new radiation is gained.

parameters.label: Radiation Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much health damage accumulated radiation causes once radiation begins hurting you, without moving the vanilla radiation-state thresholds.

notes: Aggregate transform over the 11 runtime radiation-damage effect prototypes; radiation thresholds remain vanilla.
The runtime values are not replaced by one universal damage number; each stage keeps its original relative value.

parameters.rationale: Controls the health damage caused by radiation after the game has already decided that your current radiation level should hurt you.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla radiation damage. 50% halves the damage at every radiation stage. 200% doubles it. The points where radiation moves into stronger stages stay vanilla.
parameters.interaction: Radiation Accumulation controls how quickly radiation builds up. Radiation Recovery and Anti-Rad control how quickly it is removed. The Master radiation bundle adds a separate stamina penalty.

parameters.label: Bleeding Effect Strength
parameters.description: Scales the difficulty-wide bleeding effect applied by sources that cause bleeding.
parameters.rationale: Scales the difficulty-wide bleeding effect applied by sources that cause bleeding.
parameters.logic: Higher values make bleeding effects stronger overall; lower values soften them. Novice uses 25%, Stalker/Veteran 100%, and Master 150%.
parameters.interaction: This is the global difficulty bleeding multiplier. The Low / Medium / Severe Bleeding Damage sliders control HP loss once those bleeding states are active, while Natural Bleeding Recovery and medical treatment control how bleeding is removed.

parameters.label: Natural Bleeding Recovery
parameters.description: Controls the player's base natural bleeding reduction rate.
parameters.rationale: Controls the player's base natural bleeding reduction rate.
parameters.logic: Higher values make bleeding fade faster without treatment; lower values make wounds persist longer.
parameters.interaction: Bandages and medkits apply direct bleeding removal independently of this passive rate.

parameters.label: Player Max Health
parameters.description: Vanilla Player.MaxHP is 100. HealthMechanics also uses a FullHP condition of 100 to stop the low-health sound path, so this control targets both values together instead of leaving the full-health threshold behind.

notes: Direct MaxHP field is confirmed; broader assumptions about the 100-point HP scale require runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Vanilla Player.MaxHP is 100. HealthMechanics also uses a FullHP condition of 100 to stop the low-health sound path, so this control targets both values together instead of leaving the full-health threshold behind.
parameters.logic: Higher values increase the player HP pool; lower values reduce it. This is a direct pool-size change, not incoming-damage scaling.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps its vanilla low-health state boundary. Other systems may also assume a 100-point health scale, so very large Max Health changes should be tested in game.

parameters.label: Passive Health Recovery
parameters.description: Controls ordinary passive health recovery on the player. Vanilla sets this to zero, so by default you do not slowly heal just by standing around.

notes: Field and vanilla value are confirmed; exact tick semantics and interaction with effect-based regeneration require runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls ordinary passive health recovery on the player. Vanilla sets this to zero, so by default you do not slowly heal just by standing around.
parameters.logic: Zero keeps vanilla behavior. Raising it adds passive healing over time.
parameters.interaction: Health Recovery Delay decides when recovery can begin. Other healing sources, such as low-health recovery and medkits, stay separate.

parameters.label: Health Recovery Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla player VitalParams define RegenHPDelayTimeSeconds = 5.

notes: The field explicitly uses seconds; the exact set of regeneration sources that honor it requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Vanilla player VitalParams define RegenHPDelayTimeSeconds = 5.
parameters.logic: Higher values postpone actor-level HP regeneration for longer; lower values shorten the configured delay.
parameters.interaction: With vanilla Base Health Regeneration at 0, this value may be invisible until a compatible regeneration path is active. Whether every RegenHealth effect honors this delay requires in-game testing.

parameters.label: Health Recovery Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales health regeneration produced by compatible recovery effects. It does not create passive healing by itself: 100% keeps full effect strength, while lower values weaken that recovery.
parameters.rationale: EnvironmentDifficulty.Regen_HP is the difficulty-level multiplier applied to compatible health-regeneration effects; it does not create regeneration on its own.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps compatible regeneration effects at full strength. Lower values weaken them; higher values strengthen them. Vanilla uses 100% on Novice/Stalker, 75% on Veteran and 50% on Master.
parameters.interaction: Passive Health Recovery is 0 in vanilla, so this matters mainly when another effect is already restoring health, such as low-health recovery.

parameters.label: Maximum Stamina
parameters.description: Vanilla Player.MaxSP is 100. This changes the size of the stamina pool itself, not regeneration speed or the cost of any action.
parameters.rationale: Vanilla Player.MaxSP is 100. This changes the size of the stamina pool itself, not regeneration speed or the cost of any action.

notes: Runtime 2.0.5 Player.VitalParams.MaxSP = 100.

parameters.label: Sprint Stops Below
parameters.description: Vanilla Player.StaminaDisableThresholds defines the Sprint state at 16.1 SP. This is the point at which the sprint-specific exhaustion rule engages.
parameters.rationale: Vanilla Player.StaminaDisableThresholds defines the Sprint state at 16.1 SP. This is the point at which the sprint-specific exhaustion rule engages.
parameters.logic: Higher values make sprint lock out earlier while stamina is still relatively high; lower values let the player sprint deeper into the stamina bar.
parameters.interaction: This threshold works together with Sprint Recovery Delay, Maximum Stamina, Sprint Stamina Drain and regeneration. It does not change sprint speed.

notes: The mapped threshold is the entry whose StateTags contains EStateTag::Sprint.

parameters.label: Sprint Restart Delay
parameters.description: The vanilla sprint disable entry uses RegenerationDelay = 1 second. It is separate from the amount of stamina required to sprint again.
parameters.rationale: The vanilla sprint disable entry uses RegenerationDelay = 1 second. It is separate from the amount of stamina required to sprint again.
parameters.logic: Higher values make exhaustion pauses last longer before recovery can resume; lower values shorten the pause.
parameters.interaction: The delay is attached to the same Sprint threshold entry as Sprint Disable Threshold and combines with Base Stamina Regeneration after the delay expires.

parameters.label: Emergency Stamina Recovery Starts Below
parameters.description: Vanilla AdditionalRegenStaminaMechanics switches into its low-SP branch below the 30 SP boundary and applies IncreaseStaminaPoints.
parameters.rationale: Vanilla AdditionalRegenStaminaMechanics switches into its low-SP branch below the 30 SP boundary and applies IncreaseStaminaPoints.
parameters.logic: Higher values allow the low-stamina recovery helper to engage across a larger portion of the bar; lower values reserve it for near-exhaustion.
parameters.interaction: The helper uses Low-Stamina Recovery Strength and Duration. Base Stamina Regeneration still exists underneath it.

notes: The NormalSP boundary is 30; the LowSPThreshold branch starts at 0 and applies IncreaseStaminaPoints below that boundary.

parameters.label: Emergency Stamina Recovery Amount
parameters.description: Vanilla IncreaseStaminaPoints is a RegenStamina effect with ValueMin/ValueMax = 10 for 4 seconds when the low-SP branch is active.
parameters.rationale: Vanilla IncreaseStaminaPoints is a RegenStamina effect with ValueMin/ValueMax = 10 for 4 seconds when the low-SP branch is active.
parameters.logic: Higher values make the emergency recovery effect stronger; lower values make low-stamina recovery closer to the ordinary base rate.
parameters.interaction: Only applies through AdditionalRegenStaminaMechanics when stamina is in its low-SP branch. Duration is controlled separately.

parameters.label: Emergency Stamina Recovery Duration

parameters.rationale: Vanilla IncreaseStaminaPoints has Duration = 4 seconds.
parameters.logic: Higher values keep the low-stamina recovery effect active longer; lower values shorten the boost.
parameters.interaction: The effect only becomes relevant when AdditionalRegenStaminaMechanics selects the low-SP branch.

parameters.label: Speed-Limited Sprint Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Applies to the internal EStateTag::SprintUnderRunSpeed state. The name indicates sprint is active while actual movement is under normal Run speed. It is not a separate player keybind. Vanilla is -0.65. The exact engine conditions that switch into this state are not exposed by the CFG and still require runtime verification.
parameters.rationale: Internal sprint-related stamina state used when sprinting is speed-limited; exact state-selection conditions are engine-controlled.
parameters.logic: More negative values suppress recovery more strongly; zero adds no state penalty; positive values help recovery. Do not read this as a separate “slow sprint” button.
parameters.interaction: Related to full Sprint, but the engine decides when SprintUnderRunSpeed is active. Encumbrance or other speed limits may be relevant, but the CFG alone does not prove the complete transition rule.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in speed-limited sprint state

notes: CFG target is confirmed; exact runtime transition into EStateTag::SprintUnderRunSpeed is not fully documented.

parameters.label: Jogging-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Applies to the internal EStateTag::Jogging state. STALKER 2 has no separate Jogging keybind, so this must not be presented as a direct player action. Vanilla is 0.00 (neutral). The exact transition into this engine state still requires runtime verification.
parameters.rationale: Internal Jogging-state stamina coefficient; exact state-selection semantics are not exposed by the CFG.
parameters.logic: Negative values add a stamina penalty in the Jogging state; zero is neutral; positive values help recovery. This is an engine state, not a dedicated input.
parameters.interaction: The engine chooses between several movement states. This control affects only EStateTag::Jogging when that state is active.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal Jogging state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::Jogging is confirmed; there is no separate player Jogging bind and exact activation semantics require runtime verification.

parameters.label: Slow-Run-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Applies to the internal EStateTag::SlowRun state. STALKER 2 has no separate Slow Run keybind. Vanilla is 0.00 (neutral). The runtime data also contains SlowRunThreshold = 0.5, but the CFG dump does not prove exactly how that threshold selects this state.
parameters.rationale: Internal SlowRun-state stamina coefficient; state-selection semantics remain runtime-test-required.
parameters.logic: Negative values add a stamina penalty in the SlowRun state; zero is neutral; positive values help recovery. Do not treat this as the game's Walk toggle.
parameters.interaction: A separate player Walk action exists, but this CFG entry is EStateTag::SlowRun, not EStateTag::Walk. The engine transition into SlowRun is not fully documented.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal SlowRun state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::SlowRun is confirmed; SlowRunThreshold = 0.5 exists, but its complete state-selection semantics are not proven.

parameters.label: Maximum Vault Height
parameters.description: In-game 2.0.5 sets Player.VaultingParams.MaxObstacleHeight = 130. The extra WAIST / EYES / ABOVE EYES points are user-facing traversal references, not engine-defined anatomical measurements.
parameters.rationale: In-game 2.0.5 sets Player.VaultingParams.MaxObstacleHeight = 130. The extra WAIST / EYES / ABOVE EYES points are user-facing traversal references, not engine-defined anatomical measurements.
parameters.logic: Higher values let the vault search accept taller obstacles; lower values restrict vaulting to lower obstacles. The slider is capped at 300 to keep the requested range around vanilla through slightly-above-eye/head traversal rather than turning this into extreme parkour.
parameters.interaction: Vault Stamina Cost still controls the SP cost of a successful vault. MinObstacleHeight, landing checks, search radius and other vault geometry remain vanilla.

notes: The CFG field and vanilla value are confirmed from runtime 2.0.5.
WAIST/EYES/ABOVE EYES are practical UI orientation points; exact reachable world geometry depends on the rest of VaultingParams and collision/animation constraints.

parameters.label: Medium-Water Stamina Drain

parameters.rationale: Player.WaterContactInfo applies WaterMediumStaminaPenalty from the Medium immersion level (vanilla threshold 31). The effect is +100% SP drain for Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump and Vault.
parameters.logic: Higher percentages make movement actions consume more stamina while moderately immersed; lower values soften the water penalty.
parameters.interaction: This changes penalty strength only. Water immersion thresholds remain unchanged.

notes: AffectedStaminaActionTypes: Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Vault.

parameters.label: Deep-Water Stamina Drain
parameters.description: Player.WaterContactInfo applies WaterStrongStaminaPenalty at High immersion (vanilla threshold 76) and also at Deadly immersion. The vanilla effect is +200% stamina drain for Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump and Vault.
parameters.rationale: Player.WaterContactInfo applies WaterStrongStaminaPenalty at High immersion (vanilla threshold 76) and also at Deadly immersion. The vanilla effect is +200% SP drain for Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump and Vault.

parameters.interaction: This does not change the water-depth thresholds or the separate deadly-water instant-death effect.

notes: AffectedStaminaActionTypes: Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Vault.
Deadly water still has a separate WaterDeadlyDamage instant-death effect.

parameters.label: Base Stamina Recovery

parameters.interaction: Movement-state values, hunger penalties and fatigue effects can reduce this base regeneration in context.

parameters.label: Jump Stamina Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a jump.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a jump.

parameters.label: Vault Stamina Cost

parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by vaulting.

parameters.label: Normal Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a normal melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a normal melee attack.

parameters.interaction: Strong melee and buttstock attacks have independent costs.

parameters.label: Strong Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a strong melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a strong melee attack.

parameters.interaction: This does not alter melee damage, only the stamina economy of the action.

parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a buttstock melee attack.

parameters.interaction: Normal and strong melee use their own stamina values.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in full sprint state

notes: Player-facing Sprint action; CFG target EStateTag::Sprint is confirmed.

parameters.rationale: Sets the player's default maximum inventory mass.

parameters.label: Extra NPC Corpse Loot
parameters.description: Chooses the extra smart-loot package added to human NPC corpses: Medicine + Ammo, Water, or None.

parameters.label: NPC Medical Loot Chance
parameters.description: Scales the vanilla item-level drop chances for Bandages, Medkits, Army Medkits and Anti-Rad carried by ordinary repeatable human NPC loadouts. It does not change stack sizes or non-medical consumables.

targets.path: medical PossibleItems[*].Chance via standard-human-only redirect manifest

notes: The audited control surface contains 58 medical Chance rows across six shared role-oriented consumable pools.
100% preserves every vanilla Chance; 0% disables those medical rolls; values above 100% multiply each source Chance and clamp at 100%.
Seven source medical rows are already Chance = 1.0 and therefore remain capped at 100% when increasing frequency.
Only 37 audited standard-human SubItemGenerator links are redirected to TCD-owned pool clones; Prologue, zombie, named/scripted and other shared consumers remain vanilla.

parameters.rationale: Medical consumables are the only standard-human consumable category with a strong vanilla difficulty signal. Scaling only their explicit Chance fields preserves food, drink, stimulant, alcohol and count semantics.
parameters.logic: 0-200% in 5% steps. Each vanilla medical Chance is multiplied by the selected factor and clamped to 100%. For example, a 30% vanilla row becomes 15% at 50%, 30% at 100%, and 60% at 200%; a 100% vanilla row stays at 100% above vanilla.
parameters.interaction: Applies only to ordinary standard-human loadout links in the audited allowlist. It does not affect zombies, named/story NPCs, Prologue NPCs, corpse override generators, traders, stash loot or medical item stack sizes.

parameters.label: NPC Dropped Ammo Amount
parameters.description: Scales AmmoMinCount/AmmoMaxCount attached to the weapon row selected for an ordinary repeatable human NPC. The ammunition follows that specific weapon.

notes: Production-only audit locks this control to the same 121 direct weapon rows across 33 repeatable standard-human loadout roots.
All 121 rows expose AmmoMinCount and an ammo maximum: 118 spell it AmmoMaxCount and three use AmmoMaxcount; the writer preserves the source spelling.
81 rows have a zero vanilla minimum and 40 have a positive minimum. Zero values remain zero under scaling. Two Prologue and four named MIK/Mykluha roots are excluded.
Runtime verification will later determine the most precise player-facing interpretation of these attached-ammo counts.

parameters.rationale: Uses the complete isolated attached-ammo surface without touching shared loose-ammo pools or inventing ammo rows.
parameters.logic: 1x preserves vanilla counts. Counts are scaled independently with round-half-up; authored zero minima remain zero.
parameters.interaction: This changes how much matching weapon ammo the NPC carries with the selected weapon. It does not choose the weapon or caliber, and it does not alter loose-ammo loot, corpse bonus loot, traders, zombies or named/story loadouts.

parameters.label: NPC Weapon Condition
parameters.description: Sets the actual minimum and maximum condition of weapons carried by ordinary repeatable human NPC loadouts. Vanilla is left untouched until this control is changed.

notes: Production-only audit locks this control to 121 direct weapon rows across 33 repeatable standard-human loadout roots.
120 rows use vanilla 25%-50% durability ranges; one row uses 35%-45%. OFF/default behavior emits no patch, so that authored outlier remains untouched.
Once either bound is changed, the selected MIN and MAX become direct MinDurability/MaxDurability values on all 121 audited weapon rows.
Two Prologue roots and four named MIK/Mykluha roots are excluded.

parameters.rationale: Uses the complete isolated repeatable-human weapon durability surface while exposing actual condition percentages instead of a hidden multiplier.
parameters.logic: Default preserves every vanilla row exactly. The UI starts at MIN 25% / MAX 50%. After a change, those two percentages are written directly as MinDurability and MaxDurability for all 121 audited rows; MIN can never exceed MAX.
parameters.interaction: Affects only weapon condition on the audited standard-human production surface. It does not alter weapon selection, ammo, NPC health, traders, zombies or named/story loadouts.

parameters.label: Stash Ammo Amounts

Each axis scales only the existing vanilla ammo MinCount/MaxCount values for that stash tier.
1x preserves vanilla stack counts.

parameters.description: Changes how many RGD-5 grenades you receive when a Basic stash successfully rolls its grenade reward. The chance to receive grenades is controlled separately.

parameters.label: Low Fatigue Aim-Time Penalty

parameters.rationale: At the Low Sleepiness state, vanilla increases aiming time by 15%.

parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla low-fatigue state.

parameters.label: Medium Fatigue Aim-Time Penalty

parameters.rationale: Vanilla raises the aiming-time penalty to +25% in the medium fatigue state.

parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla medium-fatigue state, replacing the low-state aiming penalty.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Aim-Time Penalty

parameters.rationale: Vanilla increases aiming time by +40% in the severe fatigue state.

parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla severe-fatigue state.

parameters.label: Medium Fatigue Reload-Time Penalty

parameters.rationale: Medium fatigue adds +15% to the reload-time effect in vanilla.

parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla medium-fatigue state. It is separate from the aiming-time penalty.

parameters.label: Flycatcher Movement Speed
parameters.description: Controls how much of your normal movement speed remains while the Flycatcher slowdown is active.

notes: Runtime CFG 2.0.5 stores FlycatcherVelocityChange as -50%. The UI exposes retained movement speed instead: CFG delta = UI value - 1.0.

parameters.rationale: Shows the Flycatcher movement effect as the speed you keep, rather than exposing the game’s negative velocity-change value.

parameters.interaction: Changes only player movement slowdown inside the Flycatcher. Projectile slowdown, HP/stamina regeneration penalties and turn slowdown remain separate.

parameters.label: Flycatcher Turn Speed
parameters.description: Controls how much of your normal look/turn speed remains while the Flycatcher slowdown is active.

notes: Runtime CFG 2.0.5 stores both yaw and pitch effects as -0.7. One UI value intentionally drives both targets: CFG delta = UI value - 1.0.

parameters.rationale: Yaw and pitch use the same vanilla penalty, so the player gets one Turn Speed control instead of two technical axis sliders.
parameters.logic: Vanilla applies -0.7 to both yaw and pitch turn-rate effects, leaving 30% of normal turn speed. 100% means no turn slowdown; 0% corresponds to -1.0 on both effects.
parameters.interaction: The same setting is applied to Flycatcher yaw and pitch so horizontal and vertical looking stay synchronized. Movement speed is controlled separately.

parameters.interaction: Razor Bleeding and Razor equipment corrosion remain separate effects. This control does not change the anomaly speed thresholds.

parameters.interaction: Razor Health Damage is independent. Movement-speed thresholds and corrosion values remain vanilla.
